title: IC first-90 operating rhythm and tool access
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Overview

Purpose: This guide is a practical, role-agnostic first-90 playbook for Individual Contributors (ICs) joining Redwood. It combines an operating rhythm (meetings, checkpoints, and progress markers) with the exact tool and account access checklist that new ICs need to be productive day one through day 90.

Scope: Applicable to ICs across engineering, product, research, and platform teams. Managers should adapt milestones to team-specific objectives and share the plan during the first 1:1. People Ops owns the baseline checklist and account provisioning timelines.

Outcomes (by day 90)
- Full access to required tooling and repositories with documented troubleshooting notes.
- Clear set of deliverables for first quarter: at least one deliverable with measurable outcome (bugfix, small feature, doc, or instrumentation item).
- Career-aligned growth conversation: manager and IC agree on 90-day impact and a visible development plan.
- Integration into team operating cadence with regular contributions to standups, planning, and retros.

Quick start timeline (high level)
1) Day 0–3: Orientation and core access
   - Complete People Ops orientation and submit equipment confirmation form.
   - Confirm SSO/MFA, VPN, and device enrollment.
   - Join primary team Slack channels, PagerDuty (if oncall), and calendar invites for team ceremonies.
2) Week 1: Foundations and context
   - Read team readmes, architecture overview, and key RFCs.
   - Shadow pair session and small starter ticket assigned.
   - Complete security and data-handling training modules.
3) Weeks 2–4: Contribution and feedback loops
   - Ship first small change (doc, test, pipeline fix, or low-risk code).
   - 30-day sync: review blockers, update onboarding checklist, and refine goals.
4) Month 2: Ownership and expansion
   - Take ownership of a small area (test suite, dashboard, or routine infra task).
   - Start a retrospective-style write-up of early observations and suggested improvements for the area.
5) Month 3: Impact and career planning
   - Deliver primary 90-day milestone.
   - 90-day review: calibration with manager; update development plan and recommended learning milestones.

Detailed tool/account access checklist (baseline)
- Identity & Security
  - SSO (Okta): account provisioned and MFA configured.
  - Device enrollment (MDM): macOS/Linux/Windows enrollment complete.
  - KMS access requests started for encryption/materials if applicable.
- Communication & Calendar
  - Slack: added to team/private channels and core global channels (announcements, all-hands).
  - Google Workspace: mailbox, calendar, Drive, and shared team drives.
- Code & CI/CD
  - GitHub: org membership, repo-level write access (or CLA process started), branch protection notes.
  - CI: build status notification in Slack for core repos.
  - Container registry access (where relevant).
- Cloud & Infra
  - GCP/AWS account with IAM role scoped to environment (dev/staging).
  - Console access gated behind approval; temporary elevated access process documented.
  - Secrets manager (Vault/Secrets Manager) read access requested for dev environment.
- Observability & Incidents
  - Grafana/Datadog: read access and saved dashboards added to favorites.
  - Logging: index and search training for service-level logs.
  - PagerDuty: oncall training and escalation steps if included on rotation.
- Product & Design Tools
  - Figma, Miro, and product analytics dashboards (Amplitude/Looker) as applicable.
- Internal Knowledge & Docs
  - Confluence: access to team pages, architecture decisions, and onboarding playbooks.
  - Shared templates: PR templates, runbook templates, and RFC template.

Minimum SLAs for provisioning (People Ops commitments)
| Item | Target | Owner | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|-------|
| Okta + MDM | 24 hours | People Ops | Push reminder if delayed after 48h |
| GitHub org invite | 48 hours | Engineering Ops | Repo-specific access may take longer (team leads) |
| Cloud dev role | 72 hours | Infra | Approvals required for sensitive services |
| PagerDuty invite | 48 hours | Eng SRE | Oncall training must be scheduled before rotation |

First-90 operating rhythm (example week cadence)
- Weekly
  - Team standup (15min): status updates and blockers.
  - 1:1 with manager (30–45min): coaching, blockers, and development.
  - Office hours with buddy/mentor (1hr): pairing and Q&A.
- Biweekly
  - Sprint planning / backlog refinement (60–90min).
  - Cross-functional sync (product + design) for active projects (30–60min).
- Monthly
  - Team retro and metrics review (90min): shape improvement actions.
  - Engineering brown bag / knowledge share (45–60min).
- End of quarter
  - 90-day review and objective calibration (manager + IC).

Role-specific onboarding addenda (short list)
- Software Engineers: local dev environment template, test harness walkthrough, and performance budget doc.
- MLEs / Applied ML: model sandbox access, evaluation harness, and dataset S3/GCS roles.
- Product: customer journey dashboards, feature flags overview, and release gate checklist.
- SRE/Infra: runbook library, service ownership matrix, and CI runner access.

Manager checklist for first-90 (quick reference)
1. Share team mission, immediate priorities, and success metrics within first 3 days.
2. Assign a buddy and schedule daily check-ins for week 1.
3. Ensure required access tickets are created and tracked (link to provisioning tracker).
4. Set an initial 30/60/90 goal sheet with measurable outcomes and examples of success.
5. Provide early feedback and document decisions in Confluence.

Handover and documentation expectations (IC responsibility)
- Create a short "What I worked on" doc for each shipped item with: problem statement, design decisions, tests added, and rollbacks.
- Maintain or update at least one runbook/RFC within first 90 days.
- Add onboarding notes to team wiki covering any setup gotchas encountered.

Common provisioning failure modes and remediation (troubleshooting)
- Missing Okta group mapping: escalate to People Ops with screenshot and employee ID.
- GitHub invite expired: engineering-ops can reissue invites; confirm email alias.
- Cloud role blocked by billing policy: Infra requires a cost-owner approval; attach request ticket.
- PagerDuty not receiving notifications: check DO NOT DISTURB settings and verify phone/SMS on file.

Templates and artifacts (quick links)
- 30/60/90 goal template (copyable): /confluence/templates/ic-30-60-90
- PR checklist and release checklist: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs/pr-and-release-checklists
- Runbook template: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/templates

FAQ (short)
Q: I don’t have access to a repo I need. What do I do?
A: File an access request in the provisioning tracker, message your manager and ping engineering-ops. If it’s blocking Day 1 work, mark the ticket as high priority.

Q: Who signs off the 90-day milestone?
A: The manager signs off the milestone after a documented demo and discussion; calibration with team lead or product partner may be requested for scope alignment.

Appendix: example 30/60/90 goal sheet (text)
- 30-day goals:
  - Complete local dev setup and ship a documentation fix.
  - Demonstrate ability to run the test suite and debug a failing CI job.
- 60-day goals:
  - Own a minor feature or stabilization task end-to-end; collect user/metric feedback.
  - Present a 15-minute learning summary to the team.
- 90-day goals:
  - Deliver primary milestone described during onboarding and propose one improvement to the team’s operating model.
